questions.question: What does WAF stand for in the context of AWS?

explanation.correct: WAF stands for Well-Architected Framework — a set of best practices to design, build, and review workloads on AWS.
explanation.why: A is also a valid AWS service called WAF but in this context we mean the Well-Architected Framework. C and D don't exist.

questions.question: How many pillars does the AWS Well-Architected Framework have?

explanation.correct: The WAF has exactly 6 pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.
explanation.why: This is a commonly tested number. Don't confuse with CAF which also has 6, but they are called perspectives not pillars.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: A paid AWS service that monitors your infrastructure
A set of best practices to design, build, and review workloads on AWS
A migration tool to move workloads to AWS
An organisational readiness assessment for cloud adoption

explanation.correct: The WAF is a framework — a set of best practices, not a service you activate. It helps you review and improve your AWS architecture.
explanation.why: A is wrong (it's not a paid service in that sense). C describes migration tools. D describes CAF, not WAF.

questions.question: Which WAF pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of cloud workloads?

explanation.correct: Sustainability is the pillar focused on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads. It was added in 2021 as the 6th pillar.
explanation.why: Cost Optimization focuses on financial costs, not environmental. Reliability focuses on uptime. Operational Excellence focuses on process improvement.

questions.question: What does CAF stand for?

explanation.correct: CAF stands for Cloud Adoption Framework — AWS's framework for helping organisations prepare for cloud migration.
explanation.why: Cloud Architecture Framework doesn't exist as an AWS term. CAF specifically helps with adoption readiness, not just architecture.

questions.question: How many perspectives does the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) have?

explanation.correct: CAF has 6 perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Operations, and Security.
explanation.why: Like WAF, CAF also has 6 components — but WAF calls them 'pillars' while CAF calls them 'perspectives'. Don't mix them up!

questions.question: Which WAF pillar focuses on 'avoiding unnecessary costs'?

explanation.correct: Cost Optimization is the pillar focused on avoiding unnecessary costs — understanding spending and maximising value for money.
explanation.why: Performance Efficiency is about using resources efficiently, Sustainability is about environmental impact, Operational Excellence is about process improvement.

questions.question: Network Hardening is about controlling access at which point?

options.text: After a user logs into the system

explanation.correct: Network Hardening controls access BEFORE someone reaches the system — it's your first line of defence at the network boundary.
explanation.why: System Hardening handles what happens after someone reaches the system. Network hardening is pre-access control.

questions.question: System Hardening focuses on controlling access at which point?

options.text: Before the network request is made

explanation.correct: System Hardening controls access AFTER someone reaches the system — what they can do, which services run, file permissions, etc.
explanation.why: Network hardening is the pre-access control. System hardening is the post-access control.

questions.question: Which CAF perspective involves HR, Staffing, and People Managers?

explanation.correct: The People perspective of CAF involves HR, Staffing, and People Managers — focused on training, communications, and change management.
explanation.why: Business involves Finance Managers and Strategy Stakeholders. Governance involves CIO and Program Managers. Operations involves IT Operations Managers.

questions.question: Which WAF pillar addresses 'ensuring a workload performs its intended function correctly and consistently'?

explanation.correct: Reliability is the pillar focused on ensuring workloads perform correctly and consistently — recovering from failures and meeting availability requirements.
explanation.why: Performance Efficiency is about resource efficiency. Operational Excellence is about process improvement. Security is about protecting systems.

questions.question: What is the core truth of security according to the session?

explanation.correct: The core truth is that security is about controlling access — deciding who can get to what, when, and how. All security tools serve this purpose.
explanation.why: Encryption, firewalls, and passwords are all tools for controlling access, but the underlying principle is access control.

questions.question: A company is deciding whether to move to the cloud and needs help preparing all departments for the transition. Which AWS framework should they use?

explanation.correct: CAF is designed for organisational readiness BEFORE and DURING migration. It covers Business, People, Governance, Platform, Operations, and Security perspectives.
explanation.why: WAF is used after migration to review technical correctness. Migration Hub is a tool, not a framework. Organizations is for account management.

questions.question: After a company migrates to AWS, they want to continuously review their architecture for security, cost, and reliability improvements. Which framework helps with this?

explanation.correct: WAF is used AFTER migration to review and improve architecture against best practices for technical correctness across all 6 pillars.
explanation.why: CAF is pre-migration readiness. Trusted Advisor and Config are specific tools, not comprehensive frameworks like WAF.

questions.question: In an AWS Security Group, you allow port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0. Which hardening concept does this violate?

options.text: Network Hardening — unrestricted access to a sensitive port

explanation.correct: Opening SSH (port 22) to everyone violates network hardening principles. SSH should only be allowed from specific, trusted IP addresses — not the entire internet.
explanation.why: Network hardening controls WHO can connect, FROM WHERE, and ON WHICH PORT. Allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH is a classic network hardening violation.

questions.question: Which CAF perspective involves the CTO, IT Managers, and Solution Architects focusing on developing cloud solutions?

explanation.correct: The Platform perspective involves CTO, IT Managers, and Solution Architects — focused on developing, maintaining, and optimizing cloud solutions and services.
explanation.why: Operations involves IT Operations Managers. Security involves CISO and Security Analysts. Governance involves Program Managers and Enterprise Architects.

questions.question: Which two pillars of WAF were specifically mentioned in the session as addressing the examples of 'high bills' and 'no recovery plan'?

explanation.correct: High bills relate to Cost Optimization (avoiding unnecessary costs) and no recovery plan relates to Reliability (recovering from failures and disasters).
explanation.why: The session specifically mentioned high bills and no recovery plan as problems WAF addresses. These map to Cost Optimization and Reliability respectively.

questions.question: An IDPS system is a key component of which type of hardening?

explanation.correct: An Intrusion Detection and Prevention System (IDPS) is a network hardening component that watches for suspicious network traffic and alerts administrators in real-time.
explanation.why: IDPS operates at the network level, detecting anomalies before they reach the system — making it a network hardening tool, not system hardening.

questions.question: The Principle of Least Privilege is most closely associated with which type of hardening?

explanation.correct: The Principle of Least Privilege — giving users only the minimum permissions they need — is a core system hardening concept related to user access control and IAM.
explanation.why: Network hardening controls network-level access. Least privilege is about what authenticated users can DO inside the system, which is system hardening.

questions.question: Which statement BEST differentiates WAF from CAF?

options.text: WAF has 6 pillars; CAF has 4 perspectives
WAF is for technical correctness after migration; CAF is for organisational readiness before migration
WAF is a paid service; CAF is free
WAF is only for security; CAF covers all areas

explanation.correct: WAF focuses on technical correctness of already-deployed workloads. CAF focuses on organisational readiness — preparing people, processes, and technology for migration.
explanation.why: A is wrong (both have 6). C is wrong (both are frameworks). D is wrong (WAF covers all 6 pillars including non-security topics).

questions.question: Which components appear in the network hardening architecture diagram from the session?

options.text: Firewall, IDPS, Core Infrastructure, VPN Gateway

explanation.correct: The network hardening architecture includes Firewall (ACLs, port blocking, geo-blocking), IDPS (real-time alerts, anomaly detection), Core Infrastructure (Router, Switch, Wireless AP), and VPN Gateway (IPsec, MFA).
explanation.why: IAM/CloudTrail/GuardDuty are AWS services, not generic components. EC2/S3/RDS are compute/storage services. The question asks about generic network hardening components.

questions.question: A startup just secured Series A funding and is evaluating whether to adopt AWS. Their CEO wants to understand the business case, their CTO wants to design the architecture, and HR wants to plan team training. Which framework addresses all these needs?

explanation.correct: CAF covers Business perspective (CEO/business case), Platform perspective (CTO/architecture), and People perspective (HR/training). It's specifically designed to address all stakeholders during cloud adoption planning.
explanation.why: WAF is post-migration technical review. Trusted Advisor is a recommendations tool. Organizations manages multiple AWS accounts. Only CAF spans all these stakeholder needs simultaneously.

questions.question: Your company runs an e-commerce platform. During a major sale event, your servers crashed because you didn't anticipate the traffic spike, costing ₹50 lakhs in lost sales. Which WAF pillar did you fail to implement properly, AND which specific AWS services would have prevented this?

options.text: Cost Optimization — use Reserved Instances and Savings Plans
Reliability — use Auto Scaling, Multi-AZ RDS, and Elastic Load Balancing
Performance Efficiency — use CloudFront and larger EC2 instances
Operational Excellence — use CloudWatch alarms and runbooks

explanation.correct: This is a Reliability failure — the workload failed to perform its intended function when expected. Auto Scaling automatically adds servers during traffic spikes, Multi-AZ ensures database redundancy, and ELB distributes traffic to prevent single server overload.
explanation.why: The system crashed under expected load — that's a reliability issue. Performance Efficiency is about resource efficiency in normal operations. Cost Optimization and Operational Excellence don't address unexpected traffic handling.

questions.question: You discover that a junior developer has been given root database access 'just in case', runs unnecessary services on the production server like FTP, and the Security Group allows all traffic on all ports. Which hardening types does each issue represent, respectively?

explanation.correct: Root database access is System Hardening (user access control, Principle of Least Privilege). Running unnecessary services (FTP) is System Hardening (service hardening). Open Security Group is Network Hardening (port and access control).
explanation.why: User permissions and service management are system hardening concerns. Security Group rules are network hardening — controlling who can reach the system from outside.

questions.question: The Sustainability pillar of WAF was added in 2021. Which of the following is an example of implementing this pillar in AWS?

options.text: Using Reserved Instances to save costs
Selecting AWS regions powered by renewable energy for workloads

explanation.correct: Selecting regions powered by renewable energy directly reduces the environmental impact of cloud workloads, which is the core of the Sustainability pillar.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances save money (Cost Optimization). Multi-AZ provides reliability (Reliability pillar). IAM policies address security (Security pillar). Only the renewable energy selection directly addresses environmental sustainability.

questions.question: A CISO joins a company planning cloud migration and needs to ensure workloads align with security control, resiliency, and compliance requirements. Which CAF perspective are they primarily responsible for?

explanation.correct: The Security perspective of CAF specifically ensures workloads align with the organisation's security control, resiliency, and compliance requirements — and is led by the CISO, IT Security Managers, and Compliance teams.
explanation.why: Business focuses on business value. Governance focuses on measuring outcomes. Operations focuses on system health and reliability. Security specifically covers compliance and security alignment.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why cloud migration is described as an 'organisational change' rather than just an 'infrastructure change'?

options.text: Because cloud costs more than on-premises
Because it requires changes to people, processes, and culture — not just technology
Because AWS manages all the infrastructure

explanation.correct: Cloud adoption requires people to learn new skills, processes to be redesigned, teams to change how they collaborate, and culture to embrace continuous improvement. That's why CAF covers Business, People, and Governance perspectives alongside technical ones.
explanation.why: Cost difference alone doesn't make it an organisational change. Hardware changes are minimal in cloud. AWS managing infrastructure is a benefit, not the reason it's organisational.

questions.question: An organisation implements VPN with IPsec tunnels and MFA for remote employees. Under which hardening category does this fall, and which network hardening component is this?

explanation.correct: VPN with IPsec tunnels and MFA is the VPN Gateway component of Network Hardening. It controls network-level access for remote workers BEFORE they reach the internal systems.
explanation.why: System Hardening is post-system-access. VPN Gateway specifically (not Firewall) handles IPsec tunnels and MFA for secure remote network access.

questions.question: A team wants to evaluate their existing AWS workload against the 6 WAF pillars and generate a report of improvement areas. What is the free AWS tool specifically designed for this purpose?

explanation.correct: The AWS Well-Architected Tool is the free AWS service specifically designed to review workloads against the WAF pillars and generate improvement recommendations.
explanation.why: Config tracks configuration changes. Trusted Advisor provides best practice recommendations but isn't WAF-specific. Security Hub focuses on security findings. The Well-Architected Tool is purpose-built for WAF reviews.

questions.question: In a scenario where a Security Group blocks all inbound traffic except port 80 from anywhere and port 22 from a specific admin IP, AND the EC2 instance has IAM roles with minimal permissions and only necessary services running — which statement BEST describes the security posture?

options.text: Only network hardening has been implemented
Only system hardening has been implemented
Both network hardening and system hardening have been implemented
Neither has been implemented because a WAF service is also needed

explanation.correct: The Security Group rules (port 80 open, port 22 restricted to admin IP) represent network hardening. The IAM minimal permissions and only necessary services running represent system hardening. Both layers are present.
explanation.why: Good security requires both layers. Network hardening protects the perimeter; system hardening protects from within. The scenario clearly shows both. WAF as a service is optional additional protection.

questions.question: Which WAF pillar is focused on 'using IT and compute resources efficiently'?

explanation.correct: Performance Efficiency is specifically about using IT and compute resources efficiently — choosing the right resource types and sizes, and scaling to meet demand.
explanation.why: Cost Optimization is about financial costs. Operational Excellence is about processes. Reliability is about uptime. Performance Efficiency is about technical resource utilisation.

questions.question: Which CAF perspective involves IT Operations Managers and IT Support Managers?

explanation.correct: The Operations perspective involves IT Operations Managers and IT Support Managers — focused on system health, reliability, and agile cloud operations.
explanation.why: Platform involves CTOs and Solution Architects. Security involves CISOs. Governance involves CIOs and Program Managers. Operations is specifically for IT Ops teams.

questions.question: Geo-blocking (blocking traffic from specific countries) is a feature of which network hardening component?

explanation.correct: Geo-blocking is a firewall feature — firewalls can implement ACLs, port blocking, AND geo-blocking to control which traffic is allowed based on geographic origin.
explanation.why: VPN handles encrypted remote access. IDPS detects intrusions. Core Infrastructure includes routers and switches. Geo-blocking is a traffic filtering feature of firewalls.

questions.question: Which of the following represents System Hardening?

options.text: Configuring a Security Group to only allow port 443
Removing default user accounts and disabling unnecessary services on a Linux server
Setting up a VPN for remote access

explanation.correct: Removing default user accounts and disabling unnecessary services on a Linux server is OS and System Hardening — controlling what's inside the system after access is granted.
explanation.why: Security Group configuration, VPN setup, and geo-blocking on firewall are all Network Hardening — they control access BEFORE reaching the system.

questions.question: The WAF Operational Excellence pillar is MOST similar to which real-world concept?

options.text: A restaurant kitchen with clear workflows, checklists, and continuous improvement processes
A bank vault with multiple locks

explanation.correct: Operational Excellence is about running systems efficiently and continually improving processes — just like a well-run kitchen with standard operating procedures, learning from mistakes, and optimising workflows.
explanation.why: Insurance relates to Reliability. A bank vault relates to Security. A fuel-efficient engine relates to Performance Efficiency or Cost Optimization.

questions.question: If WAF has Pillars and CAF has Perspectives — which option correctly matches each framework to its primary timing of use?

options.text: WAF: before migration; CAF: after migration
WAF: after migration; CAF: before/during migration

explanation.correct: WAF is used after you're already in AWS to review technical correctness. CAF is used before and during migration to ensure organisational readiness.
explanation.why: This is the most fundamental WAF vs CAF distinction. Getting this right in the exam is critical.

questions.question: According to the session notes, what problem does the Well-Architected Framework help solve after migration?

options.text: High bills, security issues, no recovery plan, poor performance
Choosing between AWS, Azure, and GCP

explanation.correct: The session specifically mentioned that after migration, companies face high bills, security breaches, no recovery plan, and poor performance. WAF provides structured guidance to address all of these.
explanation.why: WAF addresses ongoing cloud health, not migration activities, hiring, or cloud provider selection.

questions.question: IPsec tunnels are associated with which network hardening component?

explanation.correct: IPsec tunnels are a key feature of VPN Gateway — they create encrypted tunnels for secure network communication between remote users/sites and the corporate network.
explanation.why: Firewall handles ACLs and port blocking. IDPS handles anomaly detection. Core Infrastructure includes routers and switches. VPN Gateway specifically handles IPsec and secure tunnelling.

questions.question: A company's CISO, IT Security Analysts, and Head of Audit and Compliance are reviewing cloud readiness. Which CAF perspective are they representing?

explanation.correct: The Security perspective of CAF is represented by CISO, IT Security Managers, IT Security Analysts, and Head of Audit and Compliance — focusing on security controls, resiliency, and compliance.
explanation.why: Operations is IT Ops Managers. Governance is CIO and Program Managers. Platform is CTO and Solution Architects.

questions.question: Which statement about the Sustainability pillar is TRUE?

options.text: It was one of the original 5 pillars of WAF
It focuses only on reducing AWS costs
It was added as the 6th pillar in 2021 and focuses on minimizing environmental impact
It only applies to large enterprise customers

explanation.correct: Sustainability was added as the 6th and newest pillar of WAF in 2021. Its focus is minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads — not financial costs.
explanation.why: There were originally 5 pillars before Sustainability was added. Financial costs are addressed by Cost Optimization. Sustainability applies to all AWS customers, not just enterprises.
